rules.statement: Turn an under-specified idea into a copyable prompt through a one-question-at-a-time interview; state the interpretation BEFORE drafting, so misalignment costs a sentence instead of a wrong prompt. (Restated in Process steps 1-2: restate in natural language with assumptions explicit, then a single focused question per turn, clarifying questions rather than a plan document; and in the Gotchas: announcing-instead-of-asking is the primary failure mode, and batching all nine questions into one message reads as a form.)
- The request is already specific (names files, behavior, success criteria) — shaping is noise; draft the prompt directly.
- The request is purely informational ("what does X do?") — there is nothing to scope.
- The user already corrected a previous interpretation — apply the correction, don't re-interview.

Emit the Spec block for sign-off: when the interview has covered every field, present the filled Spec block - a '## Spec' heading with nine bold-labeled fields in fixed order (Goal, In scope, Out of scope, Assumptions, Success criteria, Output format, Audience, Grounding context, Failure cases) - and ask the user to confirm or correct it; the interview converges on user sign-off, not on your confidence. (The Spec Block section is the template for this artifact; Process step 2's 'Elicit each field explicitly' list is the field source.)

Emit the prompt on confirmation: write the complete prompt text in a single code fence, encoding every Spec field; the deliverable is the prompt artifact itself - never execute the task the prompt describes (stated in the intro paragraph); keep it model-agnostic, omitting few-shot exemplars, chain-of-thought scaffolding, and role personas unless the user explicitly requests a technique; a confirmed spec with no emitted prompt is a failed run (Gotcha). The prompt is always emitted after sign-off, in one fence.

excluded.statement: 0. **Ground in context** — Before asking anything, scan the environment for existing patterns that inform reasonable defaults, what the prompt must integrate with, and constraints the user didn't state but likely expects. Never ask a question the codebase already answers.
